title: extractBetween
summary: Extract substrings between boundary markers in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Runs on the CPU. Documented positions are host values; resident position gathering and broader implicit broadcasting are independently gated RunMat extensions.

description: `extractBetween(text, start, stop)` returns text between two boundary markers. Numeric positions accept single, double, and all eight integer classes as one-based structural controls.
behaviors: Documented text input is a string array, character vector, or cell array of character vectors. String input returns string output; character-vector and cellstr input return cell arrays of character vectors.
Boundary inputs can be text or numeric positions. Both boundaries in a call must use the same kind of input; mixing text and numeric markers raises a size/type error.

Scalar boundaries apply to every text element. Nonscalar boundaries must have exactly the same shape as the text input in strict compatibility mode; broader implicit broadcasting is a RunMat extension.

The `'Boundaries'` name-value pair controls inclusivity. Text markers default to **exclusive** extraction, while numeric positions default to **inclusive** behaviour. Values are case-insensitive and must be `'exclusive'` or `'inclusive'`.
Missing string scalars propagate: if the text, start marker, or end marker is `<missing>`, the result is also `<missing>`.
When the start or end boundary cannot be located, `extractBetween` returns an empty string (or an appropriately padded empty row for character arrays).

Numeric positions use 1-based indexing and are read directly from native single, double, or integer storage. Inputs must be positive integers; stop positions beyond the text length are clamped by the current implementation.

Row-wise character matrices, cells containing string scalars, and resident numeric positions are separately declared RunMat extensions. Integer, logical, and complex text inputs reject before provider access.

examples.description: Extract text between words in a string
examples.input:
txt = "RunMat accelerates MATLAB workloads";
segment = extractBetween(txt, "RunMat ", " workloads")

faqs.question: Which argument types does `extractBetween` accept?
faqs.answer: The documented first argument is a string array, character vector, or cell array of character vectors. Boundaries can be text or numeric positions. Numeric positions accept single, double, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint8, uint16, uint32, and uint64. RunMat extension mode additionally admits row-wise character matrices and broader text cells.

faqs.question: Can the start and end arguments mix text and numeric positions?
faqs.answer: No. Both boundaries must be text markers or both must be numeric positions. Mixing types raises a size/type error, mirroring MATLAB.

faqs.question: What happens when a boundary is not found?
faqs.answer: The current RunMat implementation returns empty extracted text. String inputs produce empty strings; documented non-string inputs produce character vectors inside cell output.

faqs.question: How does `'Boundaries','inclusive'` behave with numeric positions?
faqs.answer: Inclusive mode returns the substring that includes both indices. Exclusive mode removes the characters at the specified start and end positions, yielding the text strictly between the two indices.

faqs.question: Does `extractBetween` support implicit expansion?
faqs.answer: Documented compatibility permits scalar boundaries or boundaries exactly the same size as the text input. Broader broadcast-compatible shapes require RunMat extension mode.

faqs.question: Are GPU inputs supported?
faqs.answer: There is no provider kernel. Resident numeric positions require RunMat extension mode, are gathered, and produce host text output. Numeric resident values are never accepted as the text argument.

gpu_behavior: Text manipulation executes on the CPU. RunMat extension mode can gather resident numeric position controls and leaves results on the host. No Accelerate provider hooks are registered, and numeric resident text is rejected before provider access.
